newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: More U.S. investment in Trinidad coming - ambassador.
newsitem.headline: More U.S. investment in Trinidad coming - ambassador.

text.p: PORT OF SPAIN, Trinidad, Nov 27, Reuter - U.S. businesses plan to invest some $3 billion in Trinidad and Tobago over the next three years, Ambassador Brian Donnelly said.
The announcement was made at the signing of a bilateral investment treaty between the Caribbean state and the United States on Tuesday.
"As the economic profile of Trinidad and Tobago rises, more and more people are coming to see what the country offers," Donnelly said.
Some 13 new companies have show interest in investing, Vishnu Ramlogan, chief executive officer of the Tourism and Industrial Development Corp told Reuters.

Donnelly said $3 billion was an extraordinary amount to invest in a country with a population of 1.3 million. He listed several reasons, including a stable government, positive economic growth, ample natural resoures and a skilled labour force.

Singing on behalf of Trinidad and Tobago, Foreign Affairs Minister Ralph Maraj said the treaty was a positive step toward joining NAFTA. Donnelly said the country was the fourth in the Western Hemisphere to have such a treaty with the U.S. The others are Argentina, Panama and Grenada.
